title: Waste Knights 2e: Beyond the Horizon - a cool expansion I can't fully recommend
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pGUjxBQqY5E

Daniel (@dungeondive) revisits Waste Knights 2nd Edition through its Beyond the Horizon expansion, and the title's hedge is earned. Post-apocalyptic Australia gains a coastline: you charter ships from port cities, with hull sizes that must match your knight's vehicle, and sail to New Guinea, Tasmania, New Zealand, Project X and Trash City for self-contained narrative encounters. A new sea encounter deck, four characters including the fully aquatic Rusalka, new scenarios and an aquatic gear trait all fold straight into the base game. He loves that — a true expansion that enlarges everything rather than sitting beside it.

Then the problems. The new board is a table hog that mostly holds cards and adds little function. Expansion content carries no icon, so separating it again means working through a list in the rulebook. And the sandbox modes, the very reason he bought this, instruct you to draw random narrative entries from a companion app that does not exist. It was pulled from the app stores before the expansion shipped, the promised publisher downloads are nowhere he can find, and BoardGameGeek threads asking where it went go unanswered.

He still praises the art, the character-specific skill decks and the nautical turn. He simply cannot recommend a box whose main mode points at missing software.

----

A retail expansion shipped in 2024 depending on an app already dead — what should a publisher owe buyers when the digital half of a physical game disappears?
